reviews.review: I just got this game to get the TF2 hat. It was kinda fun. 5.8/10

Usually, you get what you pay for when it comes to free stuff. But it was an extraordinary move on Valve's part to offer Alien Swarm for free on their popular gaming client Steam. Valve has never failed to produce an insanely fun multi-player and co-op game. With the developer's high quality reputation in mind, I had a feeling this would be a great game, even before downloading. Did I mention it's FREE!

When you load up the game, you're given several options. You can play online with friends, with randoms in a public game, or in a dedicated server. There's also an offline mode, where bots stand in for your team mates. [But obviously the best way to play this game is with your friends. While public forums are a great place to get started, you are more likely to run into issues with finding serious players. Granted this is typical of most online co-op games, it also makes balancing the teams more difficult. ..Though I'll say, I have made some interesting gaming buddies through the public lobby.]


The interface is pretty standard, offering clear navigation through the character classes and weapons. You can also navigate through character bios and mission story. If you care to read through the story, there's a brief introduction to the plot line that is touched upon by means of PDA entires sprinkled throughout the levels. I got through 2 PDA entries before deciding '...this is stupid'.  The overall storyline is pretty thin and not very compelling, but, thankfully, skipping through it won't impede your enjoyment of the game. 

The game lobby is a place for you and your team to sort out your mission and strategy. Anyone on your team can draw out a suggested course on the map for all to see. This is a great tool to keep your party on track. It also doubles as an awesome and ridonkulous way to entertain each other by scribbling random funny pictures on it. 

Your team has the choice between four classes (officer, special weapons, medic and tech) and 8 different characters. Each character has their own special abilities, strengths and weaknesses. You'll learn pretty quickly that balancing out your team is key to completing a mission and that it's nearly impossible to complete without a tech
or a medic. As for the techs, they play a particularly important role in moving the team forward. They're the only ones who can unlock doors and objectives in the game. Most of these objectives are unlocked through puzzle based minigames which puts major pressure on the person playing the tech. If the tech dies before the mission is complete, you will have to restart the level. This can be a huge pain in the ass, especially if your tech hasn't a clue what he's doing. The medics are also extremely important. Once you die during a level, you're down for the count. There is no respawn, which really focuses the challenge on the team surviving. Working together as a team is the key to getting everyone through a mission alive. While I've come across people who find these issues take the fun out of it, I, personally, love the challenge and praise the developers for giving the incentive to stay alive.  The only drawback to the no respawn system is that once you die, you find yourself sitting around twiddling your thumbs until your team either completes the level or dies.  

One of the best features of this game is the extensive weapons inventory list. There are so many great weapons to chose from. Not all the weapons are available to you at the start. There's a ranking system in which new weapons are unlocked as your character gains a level. You can max out your leveling at 27 but as you play through
again and again, you can gain medals for each time you reach the top level. Along with unlocking new weapons, you can also unlock 64 fun achievements. I'm still working on my 'Timor Station Speed Run' achievement which will unlock if I can complete the final stage within 4:25 without any marines dying. Insane? Yea, just a little!

Valve spared no detail in creating the graphics for this game. The visuals are top-notch! Even on just normal settings, the game looks gorgeous. Dynamic lighting allows the player to really get drawn into the ominous industrial atmosphere of the game. The weapon blasts and swarm effects are brutal. Alien Swarm is as much fun to look at as it is to play. 

Ammunition is priceless. You find yourself constantly trying to find ways to conserve ammo. Whenever you reload your weapon you discard any ammo left in the old clip. So you must be actively aware of exactly how much ammo you have and only reload once you are out. Being a big FPS player myself, one who unconsciously always hits the reload button, found this to be the biggest annoyance of all time! 

The game play itself is pretty repetitive, but it is by no means boring. If you like to have fun with friends, then this is the game for you. Between the various weapons/character combos you can choose to play, possible achievements and who you're playing with, the game has a pretty high replay value, despite the repetitive gameplay.  My only major criticism is that a version has not been released for Mac users. This is a bit unfortunate as it would have been a great stepping stone to get those Mac users on to Steam.

In a nutshell, Alien Swarm is a fantastic game and a must have for any gamer. And for the price of absolutely FREE, you can't go wrong. So, grab some friends and happy shooting!

Alien Swarm is a lost gem in my eyes, it is a top down horde shooter most fun with friends. It is significantly lacking in campaigns though. It was originally going to get more content but it never took off so it was abandoned by valve. I recommend getting the fan re-release with more content and a workshop Alien Swarm: Reactive drop, but with both versions the game has some bugs concerning launching the game I will not talk about solutions though you can find a guide on that. You can also get a cool TF2 hat if you beat 2 COOP missions.
